Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 1:

(p-255) Surat at-Taghabun

Medinan, with disagreement concerning it; its verses are eighteen.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah⌋ — that is, all the created beings in them both glorify Him, exalting Him, far above what is not befitting to the majesty of His presence, with a continuous glorification.

﴿To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs the praise﴾ — not to anyone else. For He is the originator of every thing, the one who sustains it, the one who watches over it, and the one who bestows the roots and branches of blessings. As for the dominion of others, it is a trusteeship from His presence, and the praise of others is an acknowledgment that Allah's blessing has flowed through their hand.

﴿And He is over all things Competent﴾ — because the relation of His essence, which necessitates power, to all things is one and the same.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 2:

﴿He it is Who created you﴾ with a wondrous creation, comprising all the foundations of perfections, both cognitive (ʿilmiyyah) and practical ('amaliyyah), along with [what is] in addition to that.

﴿So among you is a disbeliever﴾ That is: so some of you, or some among you, is one who chooses disbelief and acquires it, contrary to what his creation calls for.

﴿And among you is a believer﴾ one who chooses faith and acquires it in accordance with what his creation requires. It was incumbent upon all of you to be choosers of faith, thankful for the blessing of creation and bringing into being, and for all the other blessings that branch out from it. But you did not do this, despite your full ability to do so; rather, you split into branches and divided into sects. The mention of disbelief first is because it is the more prevalent among them, and the more fitting to the context of rebuke. Its meaning may be taken as: "So among you is a disbeliever" whose disbelief is predestined, toward which what drives him to it is directed; and "among you is a believer" whose faith is predestined, guided to what calls him to it, which is not suitable to the context.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ so He will recompense you for it. So choose from Him what benefits you of faith and obedience, and beware of what ruins you of disbelief and disobedience.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 3:

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾ with the far-reaching wisdom that includes both religious and worldly benefits.

﴿And He shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾ in that He brought you into being in the most excellent form, and deposited in you of the faculties and perceptions, both outward and inward, that are tied to the manifest and latent perfections. He adorned you with the choicest of the attributes of His creatures, singled you out with the essence of the special qualities of His originated beings, and made you the model of all His creatures in this mode of existence.

﴿And to Him is the final return﴾ in the next mode of existence, not to any other, whether independently or in partnership. So make your inner selves good by using those faculties and perceptions for that for which they were created.

﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ of matters both universal and particular, and of states both manifest and hidden. (p-256) ﴿And He knows what you conceal and what you disclose﴾. That is: what you conceal among yourselves and what you make apparent of matters. Its explicit mention, although it is already included in what precedes, is because it is that upon which recompense revolves. So in it there is emphasis on the promise and the threat, and reinforcement of both. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Knower of what is in the breasts﴾ is an interjected concluding remark (i'tiraz tadhyili, a parenthetical clause that closes a passage) confirming what precedes concerning the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of their secret and their open matters. That is: He encompasses all the concealed thoughts lodged in the breasts of people, such that they never depart from them at all. How, then, could what they conceal and what they disclose be hidden from Him? The repetition of the Divine Name (izhar al-jalala) is to indicate the reason for the ruling and to emphasize the independence of the sentence. It has been said: the affirmation of power is placed before the affirmation of knowledge because the created things indicate His power directly, and indicate His knowledge through the perfection found in them and their specific features in certain respects.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 5:

﴿Has there not come to you﴾ O disbelievers.

﴿the news of those who disbelieved before﴾ like the people of Noah and those after them among the nations persisting in disbelief.

﴿So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾ This is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with "disbelieved." Al-wabāl (evil consequence) is the heaviness and severity that follows from a matter. Their affair, which is their disbelief, is expressed by this to signal that it is a monstrous matter and a great crime. That is: has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before, so that they tasted, without delay, what their disbelief entailed in this world?

﴿And for them﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿is a painful punishment﴾ whose extent cannot be measured.

**﴿ذَلِكَ﴾** That is, what was mentioned of the punishment that they tasted in this world and what they will taste in the Hereafter.

**﴿بِأنَّهُ﴾** Because, by reason of the fact that the matter (ash-sha'n)...

**﴿كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهم بِالبَيِّناتِ﴾** That is, with the manifest miracles (al-mu'jizat, the miracles).

**﴿فَقالُوا﴾** This is conjoined (ʿatf) upon "kānat" (was coming).

**﴿أبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا﴾** That is: each people of those mentioned said, regarding their messenger who came to them with the miracles, denying that the messenger could be of the kind of mankind (al-bashar) and marveling at that: "Is it a human (basharun) who guides us?" just as Thamud said, "A single human (basharan) from among us, whom we would follow?" The speech was summarized in the narration, so the saying was attributed to all the peoples, and "al-bashar" is intended as a genus, so it was described with the plural, just as the address was summarized. And the command in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الرُّسُلُ كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ واعْمَلُوا صالِحًا﴾ [O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds] (is similar).

**﴿فَكَفَرُوا﴾** That is, in the messengers.

**﴿وَتَوَلَّوْا﴾** They turned away from reflecting upon what they brought of the manifest signs, and from believing in them.

**﴿واسْتَغْنى اللَّهُ﴾** That is, He manifested His independence from their faith and obedience, in that He destroyed them and cut off their last trace. Had He not been free of need of both, He would not have done that.

**﴿واللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ﴾** Free of need of the worlds, much less of their faith and obedience.

**﴿حَمِيدٌ﴾** Praised by every creature through the tongue of its condition (bi-lisan al-hal), or deserving of praise in His essence, even if no one praises Him.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 7:

﴿The disbelievers claimed that they would never be resurrected.﴾ Al-za'm (claim) is the pretension to knowledge, and it transitively takes two objects, and the light (mukhaffafah) form of "anna" together with what falls within its scope has taken the place of both of them. What is meant by the relative pronoun is the disbelievers of Makkah; that is, they claimed that the matter was that they would never be resurrected after their death, ever.

﴿Say﴾ in response to them and in refutation of their claim, by affirming what they had denied.

﴿Yes indeed﴾ meaning: you will be resurrected. And His saying: ﴿By my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did﴾ means: you will surely be called to account and recompensed for your deeds. This is an independent sentence (p-257) placed under the command, brought to emphasise what the word "Yes" conveyed of affirming the resurrection, and to state the certain occurrence of another matter that branches from it and is contingent upon it. Thus there is emphasis on the certainty of the resurrection in two respects.

﴿And that﴾ means: what has been mentioned of resurrection and recompense.

﴿is easy for Allah﴾ because of the complete power and the receptivity of the substance being certain.

The fa' in His words ﴿So believe﴾ is an eloquent fa' (fa' faṣīḥa), which reveals an omitted condition, relying on how plainly it is understood. The meaning is: if the matter is as such, then believe.

﴿in God and His Messenger﴾ — Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿and the light which We have sent down﴾ — this is the Qur'an, for by its inimitability it is manifest in itself and makes other things manifest, just as light does. The shift to the plural "We" (nūn al-ʿaẓama, the royal "we") serves to display the complete care given to the matter of the sending down.

﴿And God is aware of what you do﴾ — of compliance with the command or its absence.

﴿Well-Acquainted﴾ — so He will recompense you for it. The clause is a parenthetical concluding statement (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī), confirming what precedes it, namely the command that makes compliance obligatory, through promise and threat. The shift to the Majestic Name (al-ism al-jalīl, Allah) serves to cultivate awe and to emphasize the independence of the clause.

ـ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ﴾ is an adverbial complement (ẓarf) governing "tunabba'unna" (you will be informed). It is said that it governs "khabīr" (All-Aware), because of the meaning of warning contained in it, as if it were said: "And Allah will reward you and punish you on the day He gathers you." Or it is an object of "udhkur" (remember). It is read "najma'ukum" with the plural of majesty (nūn al-'aẓama).

﴿لِيَوْمِ الجَمْعِ﴾ for a day on which the first and the last will be gathered, i.e., for the sake of what it contains of reckoning and recompense.

﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ﴾ That is, it is a day of mutual deception (ghabn) among people, through the descent of the happy into the places of the wretched had they been happy, and the reverse. In the hadith: "No servant enters Paradise except that he is shown his seat in the Fire, had he done evil, so that he may increase in gratitude; and no servant enters the Fire except that he is shown his seat in Paradise, had he done good, so that he may increase in regret." The specification of mutual deception (taghābun) to that day is to indicate that the true mutual deception is what occurs on it, not what occurs in worldly affairs.

﴿وَمَن يُؤْمِن بِاللَّهِ ويَعْمَلْ صالِحًا﴾ That is, a righteous deed.

﴿يُكَفِّرْ﴾ That is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is read with the plural of majesty (nūn al-'aẓama).

﴿عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿وَيُدْخِلْهُ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أبَدًا﴾ It is read "nudkhiluhu" with a nūn.

﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ That is, what has been mentioned of the expiation of misdeeds and the admission into the Gardens.

﴿الفَوْزُ العَظِيمُ﴾ the triumph beyond which there is no triumph, since it encompasses deliverance from the greatest of destructions and attainment of the most exalted aims.

﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — they are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally. And wretched is the destination.﴾ That is: the Fire. It is as if these two noble verses are an explanation of the manner of the mutual loss (al-taghabun).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 11:

﴿No affliction befalls [anyone]﴾ — of the worldly afflictions (masa'ib, "calamities").

﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾ — i.e., by His decree (taqdir) and His will, as though the affliction itself were directed toward the human being while being contingent upon His permission, may He be exalted.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart﴾ — at the time of its occurrence, to steadfastness (thabat) and to returning to Allah (istirja'). It has also been said: He guides his heart until he knows that what befell him would not have missed him, and what missed him would not have befallen him. It has also been said: He guides his heart, i.e., He is gentle with him and expands his breast (yashrahu) for increased obedience and good. It has been read as "yuhda qalbuhu" in the passive voice with "qalbuhu" in the nominative; it has been read with "qalbahu" in the accusative, following the pattern of "safiha nafsahu" ("he was foolish about himself"). It has also been read "yahda' qalbuhu" with a hamza, meaning: his heart becomes tranquil (yaskun).

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾ — among the things of which the hearts and their states are a part.

﴿Knowing﴾ — so He knows the faith of the believer and guides his heart to what has been mentioned.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 12:

﴿And obey Allah, and obey the Messenger﴾. He repeated the command for emphasis, and to signal the difference between the two obediences in their mode, and to clarify the object of turning away in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., from obeying the Messenger. His words, Exalted is He: ﴿then the duty of Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾ are a justification for the omitted answer, i.e., "then there is no blame upon him, since his only duty is the clear conveyance," and he has fulfilled that in a manner beyond which nothing more can be asked. The mention of "the Messenger" explicitly, with the plural of majesty ("Our"), in place of a pronoun, is to honor him, upon him be blessings and peace, and to indicate the basis of the ruling, which is that his function, upon him be blessings and peace, is purely conveyance, and to increase the reprehensibility of turning away from him.

﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him.﴾ This is a nominal sentence consisting of a mubtada' (subject) and khabar (predicate) (grammatical subject and predicate). That is, He alone deserves to be worshipped (al-ma'budiyya), and no other. There is a well-known disagreement among the grammarians (al-nuhat) concerning whether the khabar of "la" (no) is to be supplied as "in existence," or as "it is possible that it exists."

﴿And upon Allah﴾ That is, upon Him, exalted is He, specifically and not upon anyone else, neither independently nor in partnership.

﴿So let the believers rely [upon Allah].﴾ The name of Allah (al-jalala) is mentioned explicitly in the position where a pronoun could have been used, to indicate the reason for reliance (al-tawakkul) and the command to it. Divinity (al-uluhiyya) requires devoting oneself wholly to Him, exalted is He, and severing attachment to everything other than Him entirely.

(p-259) ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾: a test and an affliction, which lead you into sin from a direction you do not expect.

﴿And with Allah is a great reward﴾ for the one who prefers love of Allah the Exalted and obedience to Him over love of wealth and children and striving to arrange their welfare.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 16:

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. That is: exert your utmost effort and capacity in being mindful of Him (taqwa).

﴿And listen﴾ to His admonitions.

﴿And obey﴾ His commands.

﴿And spend﴾ from what He has provided you, in the channels in which He has commanded you to spend, sincerely for His sake.

﴿It will be better for yourselves﴾. That is: do good for your own souls and do what is better and more beneficial for them. This is an emphasis urging compliance with these commands and an explanation that the matters mentioned are better for their souls. It is also permissible for it to be an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning "spending that is good," or the predicate of an omitted *kāna* (it was/will be), meaning as an answer to the commands: "it will be good for your souls."

﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, those are the successful﴾, the ones who attain every desired goal.

If you lend to Allah a good loan, [meaning: by directing your wealth to the channels He has designated], ﴿a good loan﴾ [meaning: accompanied by sincerity and a willing soul], ﴿He will multiply it for you﴾ [meaning: from one to ten, up to seven hundred and more], and it has been recited as "yuḍa'‘if-hu lakum" (yuḍa''if-hu lakum). ﴿And forgive you﴾ [meaning: through the blessing of spending, any of your sins that have passed]. ﴿And Allah is Grateful﴾ [meaning: He gives abundantly in return for a meager little]. ﴿Forbearing﴾ [meaning: He does not hasten punishment despite the abundance of your sins].

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 64, verse 18:**

﴿ʿĀlim al-ghayb wa-l-shahāda﴾ (Knower of the unseen and the witnessed): nothing whatsoever is hidden from Him.

﴿al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm﴾ (the Almighty, the All-Wise): the one who reaches the utmost in power and wisdom.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Taghabun, the sudden death will be warded off from him."
